CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Part One
Rights of Female Victims

Article 17
(1) Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various actions:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
(2) Every form of threatening action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, whether carried out verbally or non-verbally, that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(3) Every form of Discrimination action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(4) Every form of Violence action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out whether physical, psychological, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(5) Every form of Exploitation action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d that is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and respect of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

Article 26
(1) Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
(2) Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency.
7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration.
8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus.
9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or gender-based discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
10. Child Victim is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without using means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trustworthy namely parents, close family, teachers, mentors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions.
17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children.
18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution.
19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives.
20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services.
21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems.
22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels.
23. Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that coordinates the implementation of an integrated Service system for Female Victims and Child Victims.
24. Social Reintegration is all efforts to strengthen the readiness and ability of Female Victims and Child Victims to regain their welfare in social, political, economic, and cultural life with dignity, including strengthening acceptance and support into the family and/or community environment for the protection and fulfillment of the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims.
25. Restitution is compensation payment given to Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families by the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families.
26. Legal Aid Provider is a legal aid institution or community organization that provides legal aid services based on laws and regulations.
27. Business World is a commercial organization, the entire industrial environment and production of goods/services, including State-Owned Enterprises, and Regional-Owned Enterprises as well as private or entrepreneurs and their networks, who will carry out their social responsibilities.

Article 36

(2) The report recipient as referred to in Article 35 paragraph (3) shall protect the reporter, victim, and witness.

That satisfies the harmful practices indicator (early/child marriage). However, none of the retrieved English candidate passages include Pasal 14, so the judge never saw the key evidence (retrieval failure). Additionally, the judge’s rationale lists early marriage as an example of harmful practices; had Pasal 14 been retrieved, a correct decision would be Yes.

1.8.rationale: Reviewing the original Indonesian regulation, it does not clearly and explicitly mention “perdagangan orang” / “perdagangan manusia” (human trafficking/trafficking in persons). The closest language is general “Eksploitasi” (defined broadly in Pasal 1 angka 15, including prostitution, forced labor, slavery-like practices, etc.) and general protection/handling provisions, plus Pasal 15 ayat (1) huruf b about “Pencegahan perdagangan perempuan dan anak” (prevention of trafficking of women and children). However, the retrieved passages for this indicator did not include Pasal 15(1)(b), and even in the full text trafficking is only mentioned once as a prevention item without further trafficking-specific definition/measures. Given what the judge saw (no trafficking mention) and the overall document’s limited trafficking treatment, the golden “Yes” is questionable; at minimum it depends on whether a single prevention clause counts as ‘addresses human trafficking’. If the rubric requires explicit trafficking mention, the golden label should be No; if it allows a single prevention clause, then retrieval failed. Based on the document as a whole, I lean that the golden label is likely incorrect or at least overstated.

3.4.evaluator_rationale: While the Integrated Service Center includes "protection services," the provided sentences do not explicitly mention shelters, safe houses, or a service unit providing accommodation-based safety/protection shelter.

3.7.rationale: The retrieved English candidates actually contain explicit psychosocial counseling content via the definition of “Pendampingan” in Pasal 1 angka 19: it includes “konseling” (counseling) and “terapi psikologis” (psychological therapy), which are core psychosocial support services. In addition, Pasal 9 ayat (2) huruf b provides child victims the right to “Pendampingan konseling” (counseling assistance), and Pasal 21 ayat (2) huruf c mentions provision of companions in “kesehatan dan konseling” if needed (though this specific Pasal 21 excerpt was not in the 3.7 candidate list, Pasal 1(19) and Pasal 9(2)(b) are enough). Despite this, the judge claimed there was no explicit psychosocial counseling service. That is a misread/overly strict interpretation given the explicit term “counseling” in the retrieved material.

6.2.evaluator_rationale: While the text defines and prohibits exploitation and provides handling/rehabilitation for female victims, none of the candidate sentences explicitly mention human trafficking/trafficking victims or set out trafficking-specific protection measures.

evidence_candidates.text:
Article 17
(1) Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various actions:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
(2) Every form of threatening action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, whether carried out verbally or non-verbally, that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(3) Every form of Discrimination action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(4) Every form of Violence action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out whether physical, psychological, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(5) Every form of Exploitation action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d that is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and respect of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Part One
Rights of Female Victims

CHAPTER VI
IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S PROTECTION
Part One
Prevention

Article 19
(1) Social security as referred to in Article 18 letter a shall be carried out by the Regional Government together with the Village/Sub-district Government, Business Community, and society.
(2) Social security as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be carried out by means of:
a. reporting if there is information of the occurrence of acts of threat of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against women;
b. implementing protection for Women Victims of acts of threat of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation;
c. conducting Assistance and empowerment for Women Victims of acts of threat, Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation; and/or
d. conducting security measures against perpetrators of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against Women who potentially endanger life safety.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency.
7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration.
8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus.
9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or gender-based discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
10. Child Victim is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without using means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trustworthy namely parents, close family, teachers, mentors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions.
17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children.
18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution.
19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives.
20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services.
21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems.
22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels.
23. Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that coordinates the implementation of an integrated Service system for Female Victims and Child Victims.
24. Social Reintegration is all efforts to strengthen the readiness and ability of Female Victims and Child Victims to regain their welfare in social, political, economic, and cultural life with dignity, including strengthening acceptance and support into the family and/or community environment for the protection and fulfillment of the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims.
25. Restitution is compensation payment given to Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families by the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families.
26. Legal Aid Provider is a legal aid institution or community organization that provides legal aid services based on laws and regulations.
27. Business World is a commercial organization, the entire industrial environment and production of goods/services, including State-Owned Enterprises, and Regional-Owned Enterprises as well as private or entrepreneurs and their networks, who will carry out their social responsibilities.

Paragraph 3
Provision of Supporting Facilities and Infrastructure for Protection of Women Article 21 (1) The provision of supporting facilities and infrastructure as referred to in Article 18 letter c aims to maximize the sense of security, comfort and peace for Women Victims of acts of threats, Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.
(2) The provision of supporting facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. provision of temporary safe houses;
b. provision of daily living needs during the process of Assistance in handling at temporary safe houses; c. provision of Assistants in the field of health and counseling if needed;
d. conducting empowerment to increase the capacity of women in the future; and e. provision of assistant personnel in the field of mental spiritual.
(3) The provision of supporting facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "the principle of humanity" is providing protection and respect for human rights, dignity, and the honor of every Indonesian citizen and specifically women and children.
Letter b What is meant by "the principle of respect and fulfillment of the rights of women and children" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.
Letter c What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination and non-exploitation" is respecting equality of status without distinguishing the parties on the basis of race, ethnicity, nationality, skin color, social status, affiliation or ideology and so forth, as well as respecting the position and honor of women and children without any utilization that is contrary to the values that exist in society.
Letter d What is meant by "the principle of harmony" is a view to live harmoniously and in balance that encourages a state of peaceful, calm, and happy relations between individuals.
Letter e What is meant by "the principle of protection" is the provision of protection to create tranquility in society.
Letter f What is meant by "the principle of justice and gender equality" is encouraging balance between rights and obligations in accordance with laws and regulations.
Letter g What is meant by "the principle of welfare" is the fulfillment of material and non-material needs.
Letter g What is meant by "the principle of proportionality" is the placement of something according to proportion by observing the situation, condition, place and time while prioritizing balance between rights and obligations.

Article 26
(1) Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
(2) Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

6.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does mention trafficking: Pasal 15 ayat (1) huruf b requires the Regional Government to conduct “Pencegahan perdagangan perempuan dan anak” (prevention of trafficking of women and children). That is the most direct basis for identifying trafficking victims as a relevant group within the policy’s scope. However, the retrieved passages for indicator 6.2 did not include Pasal 15(1)(b) and mostly covered general discrimination/violence/exploitation handling. Because the trafficking-specific clause was not surfaced to the judge, the system produced a false negative due to retrieval failure.
